author: cam
body: IrNegate constant fold (CL 1003) must preserve the outer AUnaryExpr span, not the inner IrIntLit span. The span anchors diagnostics to the source negation site.

author: blu
body: Without the set, a shadow answered two ways in one function: the fold caught `text-length "abc"` and gave the builtin's answer, while `text-length (substring "abcde" 0 3)` reached `emit-compound`, which checks `user-arity < 0` before routing to `emit-builtin` and so gave the definition's. Same name, same body, different answers, decided by whether the argument happened to be a literal. This was first recorded as a per-builtin split -- `text-length` shadowed and `abs` not -- and it is really a per-CALL-SITE split, which is why `abs` looked fine: nothing folds `abs`.

author: blu
body: Phase 2 of inlining. Leaf inlining above will only take a body of pure integer arithmetic over the callee's own parameters, because it inlines at EVERY call site and so pays for the body once per site. A definition referenced exactly ONCE in the whole chapter does not have that problem: substituting it duplicates nothing, and once the single reference is gone the definition is unreachable and emit-time dead-code elimination drops it. So the body vocabulary can widen where the caller count cannot.

author: blu
body: Worth recording that the first reading of those numbers was wrong. Deck unchanged was reported as "does nothing", which is one metric standing in for a conclusion it cannot support -- the deck measures what the pass ALLOCATES, and the point of the pass is what the emitter then does not have to write.

author: blu
body: Everything else is the single-caller pass's machinery, reused rather than restated: the same binder-free allow-list (`once-binder-free`), the same arity band, the same census (`count-refs-chapter`), and the same site admission (`once-apply-site`: saturated arity, simple arguments, the shadowed-free-name capture guard). The only new judgment is the cost function and who qualifies: a reference count of TWO or more, because a count of one belongs to the single-caller pass that ran just before and a count of zero is dead already. A candidate whose sites all inline loses its last reference and emit-time dead-code elimination drops the definition; one with a declining site (a bare reference, a partial application) simply stays.
